chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I said: A man forgets the recitation in the first two rak'ahs, then remembers in the last two rak'ahs that he did not recite. He said: Has he completed the ruku' and the sujud? I said: Yes. He said: Indeed, I dislike that I should make the end of my salat its beginning.

key_terms.صَلَاتِي: my prayer; here referring to the structure of salat
key_terms.ٱلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ ٱلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the last two units of the prayer
key_terms.ٱلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ ٱلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ: the first two units of the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they forgot the recitation in the first two rak'ahs of salat and remembered later?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who forgets the recitation in the first two rak'ahs of salat and only remembers in the last two. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام indicates that once the prayer has advanced past ruku' and sujud, he does not approve of turning the latter part of the salat into the former, pointing to the maintenance of the prayer's proper order.
